Schemme, S., Breuer, J.L., Koller, M., Meschede, S., Walman, F., Samsun, R.C., Peters, R. and Stolten, D. (2020). H2-based synthetic fuels: A techno-economic comparison of alcohol, ether and hydrocarbon production. International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, 45(8), 5395-5414. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhydene.2019.05.028 (DOI printed on the manuscript; volume, issue and pages from to-get.csv, not printed; manuscript received 15 Feb 2019, accepted 3 May 2019).

Page numbers are the manuscript page numbers printed at the foot of each page (Table 3 on p.20, Tables A1-A2 on p.29); PDF page = printed page. Data are Germany-centred Aspen Plus simulations (not a region-specific market), 300 MW fuel output, 8000 h/a, base case H2 4.6 EUR/kg and CO2 70 EUR/t, for 12 H2+CO2 routes (methanol, ethanol, 1- and 2-butanol, iso-octanol, DME, OME1, OME3-5 routes A/B/C, MTG gasoline, FT diesel and kerosene). Loaded: TRL, capex (EUR/kW fuel LHV), cost of manufacturing (EUR/l diesel equivalent; plus EUR/kg for methanol and DME), three efficiencies (ETA_LHV, ETA_Plant, ETA_PTL as three rows with distinguishing target), H2 and CO2 input per kg fuel as flows (Table A1), 20-year life and 8000 h/a as capacity factor. Not loaded: energy demand per lDE (chart-only Figure 2) and cost split (Figure 3, chart-only), the Supplementary Material (not in file). Traps: (1) system boundary excludes H2 and CO2 supply, so the numbers are the synthesis plant only, but every route includes its upstream synthesis steps (for example ethanol includes methanol and DME). (2) No price year is printed: 2020 flagged. (3) Methanol-to-jet is not a route in this paper; jet fuel appears only as FT-SPK kerosene. (4) Table 3 prints kgH2/lDE 0.270 for OME1 but Table A1 gives 0.410 (0.270 is the kg/kg value); OME1 LHV 19.92 MJ/kg duplicates methanol. (5) Table 3 prints a single cost (2.303) and capex (666.6) spanning the FT diesel and kerosene columns. (6) Route C capex (1625.5) and cost (3.96) come from the text and abstract; route B has neither. (7) CAPEX accuracy is -30%/+50% (AACE). (8) Efficiencies are printed as fractions and converted to % with formula.
